measured: Application calls and optional settings are recorded below at the cited commits.

applications.name: open-autonomy-org/open-autonomy (Open Autonomy, the Hermes kit)
applications.client: setup: fetch with Bot DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN at https://discord.com/api/v10 (packages/kit-hermes/src/setup.ts); the agent: Hermes (hermes-agent v2026.8.31, its Discord adapter on discord.py 2.7.1; rows marked hermes-agent: and discord.py:, or hermes-agent@v2026.8.31: and discord.py@2.7.1:, are those packages' paths at those versions), started by the kit as `hermes gateway run` with the token setup saves

backend.call: setup checks the bot's application against the project's branding (name, id)
setup checks the home channel is a server channel (id, guild_id)
the kit starts Hermes's gateway with the saved token and home channel
Hermes logs in: discord.py reads the bot's own user
...and its application (owner, flags)
Hermes opens the Gateway at Discord's own host, wss://gateway.discord.gg/
once READY, Hermes reconciles its slash commands (on every start; DISCORD_COMMAND_SYNC_POLICY "safe" by default): it lists the application's global commands
...deletes the ones it no longer has, first
...creates each one the application lacks, 4.5 seconds apart
...and edits one whose name, description or options differ (name, description and options sent)
a message that names the bot is marked 👀 while Hermes works
Hermes shows it is typing, every 12 seconds while it works
a mention opens a thread on the message (auto-thread, on by default)
the answer, and its progress message, posted in the thread
the progress message edited in place as the agent works
the 👀 taken back when the turn ends
...and ✅ (or ❌ when the turn failed) put in its place
a scheduled job's report to the home channel: the channel read when not cached, then the post
a person invokes a registered command or clicks a confirmation's button; the Gateway delivers INTERACTION_CREATE

Hermes acknowledges a slash command with an ephemeral deferred response, or refuses an unauthorized invoker privately; a confirmation's button click edits the prompt (its embed and its buttons disabled)
a slash command that needs confirming (/reload-mcp) posts its prompt: the text, an embed and Approve Once, Always Approve and Cancel
the command acknowledgement replaces the deferred response
commands without acknowledgement text delete the deferred response
a confirmation's result sent as a followup after the button resolves it

applications.name: volter-ai/supercode (Volter Harness)
applications.client: the Chat SDK's Discord adapter (@chat-adapter/discord 4.39.0, discord.js on the Gateway, fetch at https://discord.com/api/v10; rows marked @chat-adapter/discord: are its published dist), Bot DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN from Hermes's .env; configuration read at sdk/orchestrator/adapters/chat-sdk.mjs:10,81,209

backend.call: the application's id and verify_key, which Hermes's env does not carry
the Gateway listener (discord.js) finds the Gateway
backend.setting: Demand in full: Volter Harness ships the Gateway listener. Its SDK follows the returned Gateway URL; the REST host discord.com must advertise the separate gateway.discord.gg socket host (@chat-adapter/discord 4.39.0, discord.js WebSocketShard.internalConnect).

backend.call: the Gateway: Guilds, GuildMessages, MessageContent, DirectMessages and both reactions; MESSAGE_CREATE is a message in, MESSAGE_REACTION_ADD a reaction heard
a mention opens a thread on the message (the adapter's handleGatewayMessage)
a reply posted in the thread, or in the channel (in parts of 2000 characters)
a message to the home channel by its bare id

applications.name: calcom/cal.diy (Cal.com)
applications.client: its webhook sender: a subscriber URL on https://discord.com/api/webhooks/ gets the Discord template (content, embeds of fields) as JSON

backend.call: the Discord template chosen for a discord.com/api/webhooks/ subscriber URL
a booking posted to the webhook

applications.name: Twin (twin-world's own callers)
applications.client: the architecture's sockets (a client finds the vendor's socket where its API says it is: Discord's GET /gateway/bot) and a World's socket steps (packages/twin-standard/src/walk/journey-kit.ts)

backend.call: a World finds the twin's Gateway where the API says it is (the architecture's sockets: "Discord's GET /gateway/bot answers the twin's own ws:// base")
a life's socket steps open the vendor's socket and speak on it (Discord's Gateway, the kit's own example)

applications.name: Twenty
applications.client: fetch (website public community counts without credentials)

backend.call: GET /api/v9/invites/cx5n4Jzs57?with_counts=true

optional.what: the Discord app's workflow tools (list the bot's servers and channels, post, edit, delete, react)
optional.setting: Install (2): add the Discord app from Settings > Applications; it is not installed as shipped (packages/twenty-apps/public/discord/README.md:27-31). Workspace creation installs only the standard application (packages/twenty-server/src/engine/workspace-manager/workspace-manager.service.ts:64-68).

optional.what: sign in with Discord (passport-discord: the authorize page, the token URL, users/@me)
optional.setting: Configuration (1): ALLOW_SOCIAL_LOGIN=true replaces false; credentials alone do not enable social login (api/server/index.js:393-394; .env.example:891).
